More generally, suppose that a point P lies on the Darboux cubic, and let A'B'C' be the circumcevian triangle of P. Define B'' and C'' cyclically. The points A'A", B'B", C'C" concur in a point, Q(P). The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that X(i) is on the Darboux cubic and Q(X(i)) = X(j): (1,991), (,3), (4,5890), (64,34815). (Angel Montesdeoca, August 3, 2021).
